observation.visible_scene: A flat, pale desert plain under a clear blue sky, with a low mountain range on the horizon and a small white cloud at the left. A white semi-truck tractor unit (cab with exposed chassis and wheels, no trailer) sits parked near the center. A large, pre-existing gray-brown dust/smoke cloud hangs over the right-middle background. The camera framing and background positions remain constant across all frames, indicating a static viewpoint.
visible_changes: Frames 1-4: the truck remains fully intact and stationary; only the background dust cloud drifts slightly.
Frame 5 (t≈0.13): a bright orange-white fireball suddenly erupts at the truck's location, completely obscuring the cab.
Frames 6-12: the fireball expands upward and outward into a triangular/rounded blast cloud; small dark fragments begin scattering radially into the sky.

Frames 13-23: the luminous fire fades into a turbulent tan-and-white dust cloud that keeps growing; larger recognizable debris pieces (cab panels, wheels, dark chunks) are seen tumbling and flying outward and upward.

Frames 24-41: the dust cloud continues to expand and rise, becoming the dominant feature; individual truck parts (e.g., a light-colored door/panel arcing high in frames 24-25, wheels rolling on the ground at right) translate away from the blast center and fall, while the cloud thickens and spreads across the original truck position.

Throughout, the explosion's center stays fixed at the truck's original ground location (expansion in place), while debris shows outward/upward translation; the pre-existing background dust cloud persists and partially merges with the new blast cloud.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or trigger of the explosion and what the truck carried or was loaded with.
The origin of the large dust cloud already present in the background at frame 1.
The final state of the debris field and dust cloud after t≈1.33s.
Whether any prior event produced the initial dust cloud.
uncertain_details: Exact material identity of the flying debris (only shapes consistent with truck cab parts and wheels are visible).
Whether the background dust cloud is moving independently or is being disturbed by the blast shockwave.
Precise timing of the truck's destruction, as the first frame already shows the fireball mid-onset.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
